# Executor Consultant Top — Top-tier Consulting Style (MBB Level)

> Common guidelines: executor-base.md. Technical constraints: shared-standards.md.

---

## Role Definition

An MBB-level (McKinsey / Bain / BCG) top-tier consulting style SVG design executor. Suitable for strategic planning, board presentations, investment roadshows, C-suite decision support, and other **premium consulting** scenarios. Core characteristics: data-driven insights, pyramid-structured narrative, extreme simplicity. Output targets C-level decision-makers.

---

## SCQA Framework (Narrative Structure)

Every MBB-level presentation follows the SCQA narrative structure:

| Element | Purpose | Typical Pages |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| **S - Situation** | Establish shared context | Cover / Pages 1-2 |
| **C - Complication** | Introduce the problem / tension | Pages 2-3 |
| **Q - Question** | The implicit or explicit question to solve | Transition page |
| **A - Answer** | Core solution | All body pages |

**Page sequencing**: Cover embodies S+C → Executive Summary answers Q → Chapters develop A → Closing revisits S

**Title writing**:

| SCQA Element | Weak Title | MBB-level Title |
|-------------|------------|-----------------|
| S | "Industry Background" | "Digital penetration surpasses 60%, industry enters deep waters" |
| C | "Challenges Faced" | "Yet three structural contradictions constrain scaled deployment" |
| Q | "Strategic Question" | "How to move from pilot to full deployment within 18 months?" |
| A | "Solution" | "Three-phase path: Focus, Expand, Scale" |

---

## Data Contextualization (Never Present Data in Isolation)

> **Golden Rule**: Never display a single data point in isolation. Every number needs context.

| Method | Pattern | Visual Implementation |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| **Time comparison** | "From X to Y" | Line chart + arrow annotating magnitude of change |
| **Benchmark** | "X vs industry average Y" | Bar chart with gray dashed baseline |
| **Competitive comparison** | "Us X vs Competitor Y" | Side-by-side bar chart, highlight own data |
| **Target gap** | "Actual X / Target Y" | Progress bar + gap annotation |
| **Ranking** | "Ranked #N of M" | Horizontal bar chart + highlight marker |

**Data annotation three essentials**: Every data visualization must include (1) The value itself (large bold font) (2) Comparison reference (baseline / prior period / competitor) (3) Meaning interpretation ("So what?")

```xml
<text x="160" y="280" text-anchor="middle" font-size="42" font-weight="bold" fill="#1E293B">97.3%</text>
<text x="160" y="310" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#64748B">Industry avg 82% | Competitor A 89%</text>
<text x="160" y="335" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#059669">Leading industry by 15.3 percentage points</text>
```

---

## Pyramid Principle (Conclusion First)

> Executives don't care about your *process* — they care about *results*.

```
         ┌─────────────────┐
         │  Core Conclusion │   ← Page title / Takeaway
         └────────┬────────┘
      ┌───────────┼───────────┐
  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐  ┌───┴───┐
  │ Arg 1 │  │ Arg 2 │  │ Arg 3 │   ← Key supporting points
  └───────┘  └───────┘  └───────┘
```

| Level | Position | Font Size |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Core conclusion | Takeaway Box | 16-18px bold |
| Arguments | Content area body | 14-16px |
| Supporting data | Charts / cards | 12-14px |

**Contrast**: Title "Market Research Results" (wrong) → "Metaverse needs 5-10 years to reach scale" (right); Body "We researched... and found..." (wrong) → "Three arguments: (1)... (2)... (3)..." (right)

---

## MBB-level Layout Patterns

### Content Page Standard Structure (1280x720)

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Gradient top bar (0,0 → 1280,6)  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Assertion title (x=40, y=50, 24px)│
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Takeaway Box (x=40, y=75,        │  ← Dark background + white text, one-sentence conclusion
│   w=1200, h=45)                  │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Content area (x=40, y=140,       │  ← Charts / data / analysis
│   w=1200, h=520)                 │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│ Source | CONFIDENTIAL | Page #    │  ← y=700, 10px
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Strategic Roadmap

Three phases laid out horizontally, `<rect rx="8">` + title + action list, `<polygon>` arrows connecting:

```
Focus Core (0-6mo)  ──>  Expand Capability (6-12mo)  ──>  Scale Up (12-18mo)
x=40,w=380              x=450,w=380                     x=860,w=380
```

### Benchmarking Matrix

Horizontal table; own row highlighted in theme color, others in gray. Leading indicators marked green, lagging marked red. Use `<circle>` or `<rect>` to build score points.

### Waterfall Chart (Change Attribution)

Start → increase/decrease factors → End. Positive factors green bars, negative factors red bars, start/end points dark bars, cumulative line as dashed connector.

---

## Strategic Use of Color

MBB-level color usage is extremely restrained — color serves information:

| Purpose | Method |
|---------|--------|
| **Focus** | Target data in theme color, everything else gray |
| **Reduce cognitive load** | Same series differentiated by opacity (`fill-opacity` 1.0/0.6/0.3) |
| **Semantics** | Green = positive, Red = negative, Gray = baseline |
| **Branding** | Gradient top bar / decorative lines in brand color |

**Commandments**: No more than 3 primary colors; accent color used at most 2-3 places globally; data series use same-hue depth variations, not different colors; background white or very light gray.

---

## Chart vs Table Selection Matrix

| Scenario | Recommended Form | Reason |
|----------|-----------------|--------|
| Comparing 2-7 categories | **Bar chart** | Visual comparison is intuitive |
| Time trends | **Line chart** | Time series clarity |
| Precise values / large rankings | **Table** | 50 data points in a bar chart would be chaotic |
| Proportional composition | **Donut chart** | More modern than pie charts |
| Two-dimensional positioning | **2x2 matrix** | Strategic quadrant analysis |
| Change attribution | **Waterfall chart** | Factor decomposition |

---

## Speaker Notes Style

### Narrative Tone

Targeting **executives / decision-makers**. Pyramid structure — every sentence carries information. Composed, authoritative, and insightful tone.

### Stage Direction Markers

| Marker | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `[Pause]` | Silence after key insight, let executives absorb | "This means we are missing a billion-dollar market. [Pause]" |
| `[Scan Room]` | Observe decision-makers' reactions, decide whether to elaborate | "[Scan Room] If there are questions, I can elaborate." |
| `[Data]` | Conversational number delivery | "[Data] 63% → nearly two-thirds" |
| `[Benchmark]` | Emphasize comparison baseline | "[Benchmark] Compared to the industry average of 12%, our 23% is nearly double" |
| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Building on the strategic framework, let's drill into the implementation path." |

### Notes Writing Guidelines

- **Pyramid structure**: Conclusion → Arguments → Details
- **Data contextualization**: Every number has a comparison reference
- **Executive language**: "The strategic implication is...", "The core insight is..."
- **Flex mechanism**: Annotate "content that can be skipped if time is tight" for flexible duration
- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core insight (2) Data support (3) Strategic implication`

### Notes Example

```markdown
# 03_strategic_path

[Transition] Having clarified the problem and the opportunity, now comes the most critical part — our response path.

We recommend a three-phase strategy. [Pause]

Phase one: Focus. Over the next six months, concentrate resources on conquering the Eastern China market.
[Data] Eastern China contributes nearly two-thirds of industry growth, [Benchmark] yet our penetration rate is only half of Competitor A's. [Pause]

Phase two: Expand. Use Eastern China as a template, replicate to Southern and Northern China.
Phase three: Scale. Leverage a digital platform for nationwide coverage.

[Scan Room] The resource allocation for phase one is in the appendix — would you like me to walk through it now?

Key points: (1) Focus-Expand-Scale three-phase approach (2) Data-backed Eastern China priority (3) 18-month full deployment
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, skip phase two and three details and go straight to financial impact]
```

---

## MBB-level Quality Checklist Supplement

### Content Level

- [ ] **SCQA complete**: Overall follows Situation-Complication-Question-Answer structure
- [ ] **Data contextualized**: Every data point has a comparison reference
- [ ] **Conclusion first**: Every page's Takeaway Box has a one-sentence conclusion
- [ ] **MECE principle**: Categorized analysis is mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive

### Visual Level

- [ ] **Color with intent**: Colors serve information delivery
- [ ] **Ample whitespace**: Not crowded; information can "breathe"
- [ ] **Visual hierarchy**: Conclusion > Arguments > Details, differentiated by font size/weight
- [ ] **Brand consistency**: Gradient top bar and footer unified throughout

### Notes Level

- [ ] **Pyramid structure**: Every page is conclusion-first
- [ ] **Stage markers complete**: [Pause] and [Scan Room] at key positions
- [ ] **Flex content annotated**: Supports flexible duration

1	# Shared Technical Standards
2	
3	Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist
8	
9	The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:
10	
11	| Banned Feature | Description |
12	|----------------|-------------|
13	| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
14	| `mask` | Masks |
15	| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
17	| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
19	| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
24	| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
25	| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives
30	
31	| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
32	|---------------|---------------------|
33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
37	
38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference
43	
44	### Presentations
45	
46	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
47	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
48	| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
49	| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |
50	
51	### Social Media
52	
53	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
54	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
55	| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
56	| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
57	| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
58	
59	### Marketing Materials
60	
61	| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
62	|--------|---------|------------|-------|
63	| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
64	| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
65	| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
66	| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |
67	
68	---
69	
70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
71	
72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)
80	
81	---
82	
83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
84	
85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
86	
87	```bash
88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
90	
91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
93	
94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
96	# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
97	```
98	
99	**Prohibited**:
100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
103	
104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
109	
110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
111	
112	### Shadow
113	
114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
115	
116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
117	
118	```xml
119	<defs>
120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
125	    <feMerge>
126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
128	    </feMerge>
129	  </filter>
130	</defs>
131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
132	```
133	
134	Recommended parameters:
135	```
136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
139	dx:             0–2
140	```
141	
142	#### Colored Shadow
143	
144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
145	
146	```xml
147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
152	  <feMerge>
153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
155	  </feMerge>
156	</filter>
157	```
158	
159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
160	
161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
162	
163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
164	
165	```xml
166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
170	<!-- Main card -->
171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
172	```
173	
174	### Image Overlay
175	
176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
177	
178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
179	
180	```xml
181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
182	<defs>
183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
187	  </linearGradient>
188	</defs>
189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
190	```
191	
192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
193	
194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
195	
196	```xml
197	<defs>
198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
201	  </linearGradient>
202	</defs>
203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
204	```
205	
206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
207	
208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
209	
210	```xml
211	<defs>
212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
215	  </radialGradient>
216	</defs>
217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
218	```
219	
220	#### Brand Color Overlay
221	
222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
223	
224	```xml
225	<defs>
226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
229	  </linearGradient>
230	</defs>
231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
232	```
233	
234	### Quick-Reference Table
235	
236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |
244	
245	---
246	
247	## 7. Project Directory Structure
248	
249	```
250	project/
251	├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
252	├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
253	├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
254	├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
255	│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
256	├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
257	└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
258	```
259

# Shared Technical Standards

Common technical constraints for PPT Master, eliminating cross-role file duplication.

---

## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist

The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:

| Banned Feature | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
| `mask` | Masks |
| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
| `textPath` | Text along a path |
| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

---

## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives

| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
|---------------|---------------------|
| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |

**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

---

## 3. Canvas Format Quick Reference

### Presentations

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| PPT 16:9 | `0 0 1280 720` | 1280x720 | 16:9 |
| PPT 4:3 | `0 0 1024 768` | 1024x768 | 4:3 |

### Social Media

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| Xiaohongshu (RED) | `0 0 1242 1660` | 1242x1660 | 3:4 |
| WeChat Moments / Instagram Post | `0 0 1080 1080` | 1080x1080 | 1:1 |
| Story / TikTok Vertical | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |

### Marketing Materials

| Format | viewBox | Dimensions | Ratio |
|--------|---------|------------|-------|
| WeChat Article Header | `0 0 900 383` | 900x383 | 2.35:1 |
| Landscape Banner | `0 0 1920 1080` | 1920x1080 | 16:9 |
| Portrait Poster | `0 0 1080 1920` | 1080x1920 | 9:16 |
| A4 Print (150dpi) | `0 0 1240 1754` | 1240x1754 | 1:1.414 |

---

## 4. Basic SVG Rules

- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

---

## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)

Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:

```bash
# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>

# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>

# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final
# Default: generates native shapes (.pptx) + SVG reference (_svg.pptx)
```

**Prohibited**:
- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`

**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

---

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

```xml
<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

#### Brand Color Overlay

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
```

### Quick-Reference Table

| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
|----------|-----------------------|-------|
| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

---

## 7. Project Directory Structure

```
project/
├── svg_output/    # Raw SVGs (Executor output, contains placeholders)
├── svg_final/     # Post-processed final SVGs (finalize_svg.py output)
├── images/        # Image assets (user-provided + AI-generated)
├── notes/         # Speaker notes (.md files matching SVG names)
│   └── total.md   # Complete speaker notes document (before splitting)
├── templates/     # Project templates (if any)
└── *.pptx         # Exported PPT file
```

## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques

> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).

### Shadow

#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended

Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
    <feMerge>
      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
    </feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
```

Recommended parameters:
```
stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
dx:             0–2
```

#### Colored Shadow

Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.

```xml
<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
  <feMerge>
    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
  </feMerge>
</filter>
```

Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.

#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback

Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:

<!-- Main card -->
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
```

### Image Overlay

#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common

Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).

```xml
<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
```

#### Bottom Gradient Bar

Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
```

#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect

Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.

```xml
<defs>
  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
  </radialGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
```

Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
```

  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <filter id="cardShadow" x="-10%" y="-10%" width="130%" height="130%">

  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#topBar)"/>

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="1200" height="52" fill="#0D1117" rx="3"/>
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="5" height="52" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="60" y="43" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">Fossil fuels still drive ~75% of global emissions — and cause 5 million+ premature deaths annually</text>

  <!-- Slide title -->
  <text x="40" y="86" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">75% of Global GHG Emissions Still Come from Fossil Fuels</text>

  <!-- === STAT CARD 1: 75% Emissions === -->
  <rect x="40" y="104" width="580" height="220" fill="#FFF7ED" rx="8" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="40" y="104" width="5" height="220" fill="#D97706" rx="2"/>
  <!-- Icon placeholder -->
  <use data-icon="factory" x="60" y="118" width="36" height="36" fill="#D97706"/>
  <!-- Big number -->
  <text x="118" y="165" fill="#D97706" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="56" font-weight="bold">75%</text>
  <!-- Label -->
  <text x="60" y="220" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">of global GHG emissions</text>
  <text x="60" y="242" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">come from burning fossil fuels for energy</text>
  <text x="60" y="264" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy</text>
  <text x="60" y="306" fill="#D97706" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">● Primary driver of climate change since the Industrial Revolution</text>

  <!-- === STAT CARD 2: 5M Deaths === -->
  <rect x="660" y="104" width="580" height="220" fill="#FFF1F2" rx="8" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="660" y="104" width="5" height="220" fill="#DC2626" rx="2"/>
  <!-- Icon placeholder -->
  <use data-icon="triangle-exclamation" x="680" y="118" width="36" height="36" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <!-- Big number -->
  <text x="738" y="165" fill="#DC2626" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="56" font-weight="bold">5M+</text>
  <!-- Label -->
  <text x="680" y="220" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">premature deaths per year</text>
  <text x="680" y="242" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">from fossil fuel air pollution globally</text>
  <text x="680" y="264" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy</text>
  <text x="680" y="306" fill="#DC2626" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">● Beyond CO₂: local air quality crisis demanding urgent action</text>

  <!-- === STAT CARD 3: Industrial Revolution dominance === -->
  <rect x="40" y="344" width="580" height="200" fill="#F0F9FF" rx="8" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="40" y="344" width="5" height="200" fill="#1E40AF" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="bolt" x="60" y="358" width="36" height="36" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="118" y="408" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="42" font-weight="bold">~200 yrs</text>
  <text x="60" y="450" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">of fossil fuel dominance</text>
  <text x="60" y="472" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">Since the Industrial Revolution, most</text>
  <text x="60" y="492" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">nations' energy systems rely on fossil fuels</text>
  <text x="60" y="524" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">● Energy systems inertia makes rapid change challenging</text>

  <!-- === STAT CARD 4: Solution === -->
  <rect x="660" y="344" width="580" height="200" fill="#F0FDF4" rx="8" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="660" y="344" width="5" height="200" fill="#16A34A" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="leaf" x="680" y="358" width="36" height="36" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="738" y="398" fill="#16A34A" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="28" font-weight="bold">Nuclear + Renewables</text>
  <text x="680" y="430" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">= The pathway forward</text>
  <text x="680" y="452" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">Rapid shift to low-carbon sources is</text>
  <text x="680" y="472" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14">essential to cut CO₂ and end air pollution</text>
  <text x="680" y="504" fill="#16A34A" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">● Renewables: solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, bioenergy</text>

  <!-- Bottom note banner -->
  <rect x="40" y="562" width="1200" height="40" fill="#F8FAFC" rx="4"/>
  <rect x="40" y="562" width="3" height="40" fill="#6366F1"/>
  <text x="58" y="587" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">
    <tspan font-weight="bold">Note: </tspan>
    <tspan>Renewable energy includes solar, wind, hydropower, geothermal, bioenergy, wave and tidal. Traditional biomass is excluded from modern renewable statistics.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="618" x2="1240" y2="618" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="648" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">Source: Our World in Data – Renewable Energy | ourworldindata.org/renewable-energy</text>
  <text x="640" y="648" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10" letter-spacing="1">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="648" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">2</text>
</svg>

📝 **Template mapping**: `templates/03_content.svg`

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewBox="0 0 1280 720" width="1280" height="720">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#FFFFFF"/>

  <!-- Top gradient bar -->
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="topBar" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#1E40AF"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#7C3AED"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <filter id="shadow" x="-10%" y="-10%" width="130%" height="130%">
      <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="5"/>
      <feOffset dx="0" dy="2" result="offsetBlur"/>
      <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.07" result="shadowColor"/>
      <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
      <feMerge><feMergeNode in="shadow"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
    </filter>
  </defs>
  <rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="4" fill="url(#topBar)"/>

  <!-- Exhibit takeaway bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="1200" height="52" fill="#0D1117" rx="3"/>
  <rect x="40" y="12" width="5" height="52" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="60" y="43" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold">Only ~14% of global primary energy comes from renewables — electricity leads, transport and heating still lag</text>

  <!-- Slide title -->
  <text x="40" y="86" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">Renewables Now Supply ~14% of Global Primary Energy</text>

  <!-- Figure image: figure_2.jpg — takes up top portion of content area -->
  <image href="../images/figure_2.jpg" x="40" y="100" width="1200" height="340" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
  <!-- Subtle overlay for image labeling -->
  <rect x="40" y="100" width="1200" height="340" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
  <!-- Image caption -->
  <text x="640" y="455" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-style="italic">Fig. 1: Share of primary energy from renewables by country, 2024 (substitution method) | Source: Our World in Data</text>

  <!-- Bottom 3 annotation cards -->
  <!-- Card 1: Global Average -->
  <rect x="40" y="466" width="370" height="130" fill="#EFF6FF" rx="8" filter="url(#shadow)"/>
  <rect x="40" y="466" width="4" height="130" fill="#1E40AF" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="globe" x="56" y="480" width="28" height="28" fill="#1E40AF"/>
  <text x="96" y="499" fill="#1E40AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="36" font-weight="bold">~14%</text>
  <text x="56" y="535" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Global primary energy from renewables</text>
  <text x="56" y="554" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">2024 data; substitution method</text>
  <text x="56" y="574" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">~1/7th of all energy consumed globally</text>

  <!-- Card 2: Regional Leaders -->
  <rect x="455" y="466" width="370" height="130" fill="#F0FDF4" rx="8" filter="url(#shadow)"/>
  <rect x="455" y="466" width="4" height="130" fill="#16A34A" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="arrow-trend-up" x="471" y="480" width="28" height="28" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="511" y="499" fill="#16A34A" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">Leaders</text>
  <text x="471" y="525" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Norway · Brazil · New Zealand</text>
  <text x="471" y="546" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Derive large shares of primary energy</text>
  <text x="471" y="565" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">from renewables (hydro-rich nations)</text>
  <text x="471" y="584" fill="#16A34A" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">● Abundant hydro resources key advantage</text>

  <!-- Card 3: Why Primary Energy Is Lower -->
  <rect x="870" y="466" width="370" height="130" fill="#FFFBEB" rx="8" filter="url(#shadow)"/>
  <rect x="870" y="466" width="4" height="130" fill="#D97706" rx="2"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-info" x="886" y="480" width="28" height="28" fill="#D97706"/>
  <text x="926" y="499" fill="#D97706" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold">Why only 14%?</text>
  <text x="886" y="525" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Primary energy = electricity + transport + heating</text>
  <text x="886" y="546" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Transport and heating are harder to</text>
  <text x="886" y="565" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">decarbonize; still reliant on oil and gas</text>
  <text x="886" y="584" fill="#D97706" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">● Electricity share (~30%) far exceeds total primary</text>

  <!-- Laggards mention -->
  <rect x="40" y="610" width="1200" height="32" fill="#F9FAFB" rx="4"/>
  <text x="56" y="631" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">
    <tspan font-weight="bold">Laggards: </tspan>
    <tspan fill="#6B7280">Fossil-fuel-producing nations in the Middle East and parts of Asia remain below 5% renewable primary energy share.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Footer -->

  <text x="471" y="584" fill="#16A34A" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold">● Abundant hydro resources key advantage</text>

  <!-- Row 2: Wind -->
  <rect x="735" y="196" width="500" height="36" fill="#F0FDF4" rx="2"/>
  <rect x="735" y="196" width="4" height="36" fill="#16A34A"/>

  <circle cx="900" cy="435" r="62" fill="none" stroke="#16A34A" stroke-width="26" stroke-dasharray="97.5 292.5" stroke-dashoffset="-85" stroke-linecap="butt"/>

  <circle cx="900" cy="435" r="62" fill="none" stroke="#D97706" stroke-width="26" stroke-dasharray="82 308" stroke-dashoffset="-183" stroke-linecap="butt"/>

  <circle cx="900" cy="435" r="62" fill="none" stroke="#9CA3AF" stroke-width="26" stroke-dasharray="27 363" stroke-dashoffset="-265" stroke-linecap="butt"/>

  <circle cx="900" cy="435" r="36" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
  <text x="900" y="430" text-anchor="middle" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">9,600</text>
  <text x="900" y="448" text-anchor="middle" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">TWh total</text>

  <!-- Donut legend -->
  <rect x="975" y="396" width="12" height="12" fill="#1E40AF" rx="2"/>
  <text x="993" y="407" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Hydro 47%</text>
  <rect x="975" y="416" width="12" height="12" fill="#16A34A" rx="2"/>
  <text x="993" y="427" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Wind 25%</text>
  <rect x="975" y="436" width="12" height="12" fill="#D97706" rx="2"/>
  <text x="993" y="447" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Solar 21%</text>
  <rect x="975" y="456" width="12" height="12" fill="#9CA3AF" rx="2"/>
  <text x="993" y="467" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Other 7%</text>

  <!-- Key insight box at bottom right -->
  <rect x="735" y="510" width="500" height="130" fill="#0D1117" rx="8"/>
  <rect x="735" y="510" width="4" height="130" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <use data-icon="chart-line" x="752" y="522" width="24" height="24" fill="#D4AF37"/>
  <text x="784" y="537" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Strategic Implication</text>
  <text x="752" y="560" fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">
    <tspan x="752" dy="0">While hydropower still leads in total output,</tspan>
    <tspan x="752" dy="20">wind and solar are growing dramatically faster.</tspan>
    <tspan x="752" dy="20">Solar generation has surged since 2010 on</tspan>
    <tspan x="752" dy="20">falling costs and policy support.</tspan>
  </text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="655" x2="1240" y2="655" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="679" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">Source: Our World in Data; Ember (2026); Energy Institute – Statistical Review of World Energy (2025)</text>
  <text x="640" y="679" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10" letter-spacing="1">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="679" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">4</text>
</svg>

  <!-- Panel background -->
  <rect x="718" y="102" width="522" height="520" fill="#F8FAFC" rx="8"/>

  <!-- Leaders section -->
  <rect x="736" y="116" width="486" height="160" fill="#F0FDF4" rx="8" filter="url(#shadow)"/>
  <rect x="736" y="116" width="5" height="160" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <use data-icon="arrow-trend-up" x="752" y="124" width="22" height="22" fill="#16A34A"/>
  <text x="782" y="140" fill="#16A34A" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Leaders: 60–98% Renewable Electricity</text>

  <text x="752" y="164" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Norway (~98%)</text>
  <text x="930" y="164" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Abundant hydropower resources</text>
  <!-- Row: Brazil -->
  <text x="752" y="186" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Brazil (~85%)</text>
  <text x="930" y="186" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Amazon basin hydropower dominance</text>
  <!-- Row: Canada -->
  <text x="752" y="208" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Canada (~65%)</text>
  <text x="930" y="208" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Hydro-rich geography + wind growth</text>
  <!-- Row: Denmark / Germany -->
  <text x="752" y="232" fill="#374151" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13">Germany (~55%)</text>
  <text x="930" y="232" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Heavy investment in wind and solar</text>
  <text x="752" y="252" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-style="italic">Denmark surpasses 60%+ from wind alone</text>

  <!-- Mid-tier section -->
  <rect x="736" y="290" width="486" height="100" fill="#EFF6FF" rx="8" filter="url(#shadow)"/>
  <rect x="736" y="290" width="5" height="100" fill="#6366F1"/>
  <use data-icon="chart-bar" x="752" y="300" width="22" height="22" fill="#6366F1"/>
  <text x="782" y="316" fill="#6366F1" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Mid-Tier: 25–40% Renewable Electricity</text>

  <text x="752" y="362" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Significant scale of investment; growing rapidly from large base</text>
  <text x="752" y="378" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">China is world's largest absolute renewable generator despite 35% share</text>

  <!-- Laggards section -->
  <rect x="736" y="404" width="486" height="190" fill="#FFF1F2" rx="8" filter="url(#shadow)"/>
  <rect x="736" y="404" width="5" height="190" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <use data-icon="triangle-exclamation" x="752" y="414" width="22" height="22" fill="#DC2626"/>
  <text x="782" y="430" fill="#DC2626" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold">Laggards: Below 10% Renewable Electricity</text>
  <!-- Middle East -->
  <text x="752" y="456" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Middle East</text>
  <text x="752" y="474" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">Saudi Arabia (<2%), UAE, Kuwait — fossil fuel exporters with</text>
  <text x="752" y="490" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">minimal renewable investment; almost entirely oil and gas dependent</text>
  <!-- Sub-Saharan Africa -->
  <text x="752" y="516" fill="#111827" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Sub-Saharan Africa</text>
  <text x="752" y="534" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">South Africa (~10%) is exception; many nations have minimal</text>
  <text x="752" y="550" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12">renewable electricity infrastructure despite abundant solar potential</text>
  <text x="752" y="572" fill="#DC2626" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">● Access gap = energy justice and development imperative</text>
  <text x="752" y="588" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">Limited investment flows + grid infrastructure deficit compound the challenge</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <line x1="40" y1="638" x2="1240" y2="638" stroke="#E5E7EB" stroke-width="1"/>
  <text x="40" y="662" fill="#9CA3AF" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10">Source: Our World in Data; Ember (2026); Energy Institute – Statistical Review of World Energy (2025)</text>
  <text x="640" y="662" text-anchor="middle" fill="#D4AF37" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="10" letter-spacing="1">CONFIDENTIAL</text>
  <text x="1240" y="662" text-anchor="end" fill="#6B7280" font-family="Arial, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif" font-size="11">8</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

[Transition] Welcome. Today we are examining one of the most consequential questions in energy policy: how far has the global renewable energy transition actually come by 2025?

This briefing draws on the latest data from Our World in Data, Ember, and the Energy Institute's Statistical Review of World Energy. We will move through the urgency of the problem, the current state of renewables in both primary energy and electricity, technology-by-technology progress, and the stark regional gaps that remain.

[Pause]

The headline: renewable energy is growing faster than at any point in history — but the pace is still insufficient to meet climate targets.

Key points: (1) Global scope — primary energy + electricity + technology breakdown (2) Data-driven, evidence-based analysis (3) The gap between progress made and progress needed
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_fossil_fuel_urgency

[Transition] To understand why renewables matter, we must first confront the scale of what we are replacing.

Three-quarters of all global greenhouse gas emissions — 75% — come from burning fossil fuels for energy. That is the foundational number driving climate policy worldwide. [Pause]

[Data] But CO₂ is only part of the story. Fossil fuel combustion also creates local air pollution that kills more than 5 million people prematurely every year. That is more than the population of New Zealand — dying annually from energy-related air quality.

[Benchmark] These figures are not theoretical projections. They are present-day realities. Fossil fuel dependence is both a long-term climate problem and an immediate public health crisis.

[Scan Room] The pathway forward is clear: a rapid shift to nuclear and renewables. This deck is about measuring how far that shift has come.

Key points: (1) 75% of GHG emissions from fossil fuels (2) 5M+ premature deaths/year from air pollution (3) Transition is urgency — not just preference
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_primary_energy_share

[Transition] So where do renewables actually stand today in the total energy picture?

Globally, approximately 14% of primary energy — roughly one-seventh — now comes from renewable technologies, using the substitution method. [Pause]

[Data] That figure reflects all energy consumed across electricity, transport, and heating combined. It is a meaningful milestone. But it also tells us that 86% of global primary energy still comes from non-renewable sources.

[Benchmark] The map on this slide shows the extraordinary variation across countries. Norway, Brazil, and New Zealand derive substantial shares of their primary energy from renewables — all driven by abundant hydropower. Meanwhile, fossil-fuel-producing nations in the Middle East and parts of Asia remain below 5%.

Why is the primary energy share lower than the electricity share we will see next? Because transport and heating — two-thirds of total energy use — are far harder to decarbonize. They still run predominantly on oil and gas.

Key points: (1) ~14% global primary energy from renewables in 2024 (2) Transport and heating lag behind electricity (3) Massive regional variation — from near-zero to majority renewable
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_generation_growth

[Transition] If primary energy shows us the full picture, electricity is where renewables have made their greatest strides.

Let me walk you through the technology breakdown of renewable electricity generation globally.

Hydropower remains the single largest source at approximately 4,500 TWh — roughly 47% of all renewable electricity. It has been generating at scale for over a century.

[Data] Wind contributes around 2,400 TWh — 25% of renewable electricity. Solar contributes around 2,000 TWh — 21%. [Pause]

[Benchmark] Here is the critical insight: wind and solar combined produce approximately 4,400 TWh — nearly matching hydro's 4,500 TWh. And unlike hydro, which has limited new sites available, wind and solar are growing dramatically.

Solar alone has increased from near-zero to 2,000 TWh in roughly 15 years — the fastest deployment of any energy technology in history.

Key points: (1) Total renewable electricity: ~9,600 TWh (2) Hydro still leads at 47%, but wind+solar now nearly equal it (3) The technology mix is shifting rapidly toward solar and wind
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 05_electricity_mix

[Transition] Zooming out to the overall electricity mix: globally, almost one-third of all electricity now comes from renewable sources.

[Data] Thirty percent. That is a landmark figure — and it is substantially higher than the 14% primary energy share, precisely because electricity is the sector where renewables have made the most progress.

[Scan Room] The world map and the country table on this slide make the disparity viscerally clear. Norway generates 98% of its electricity from renewables. Brazil: 85%. Canada: 65%. These countries benefit from decades of hydropower investment.

[Benchmark] Compare that to Saudi Arabia at less than 2%. Or the many Sub-Saharan African and Middle Eastern nations below 10%. These are not small differences in degree — they are categorical differences in energy systems.

The world average of 30% masks this extreme variance. For policy purposes, the average matters less than the distribution.

Key points: (1) ~30% global renewable electricity share in 2025 (2) Leaders: Norway 98%, Brazil 85%, Canada 65% (3) Laggards: Saudi Arabia <2%, many African/Middle Eastern nations <10%
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_hydropower_largest

[Transition] Let's examine each technology individually. We begin with hydropower — the foundation of the renewable story.

Hydropower generates approximately 4,500 TWh globally — nearly half of all renewable electricity. China, Brazil, and Canada are the dominant producers.

[Data] This is a technology that has been reliable for over a century. It provides dispatchable baseload power, which solar and wind cannot always do. That makes it uniquely valuable for grid stability.

[Pause]

But here is the strategic constraint: hydropower's growth potential is fundamentally limited. The best large-scale sites have already been developed. Environmental concerns — river ecosystems, community displacement — constrain new large dam construction.

[Benchmark] The strategic implication is that the renewable electricity mix of the future must be built primarily on wind and solar, not on further hydro expansion. Hydro is a foundation, not a growth engine.

Key points: (1) ~4,500 TWh / ~47% of renewable electricity from hydro (2) China, Brazil, Canada lead (3) Growth ceiling reached — future expansion limited
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_wind_solar_fastest

[Transition] Which brings us to the most dynamic part of the energy transition story: wind and solar.

Wind now generates approximately 2,400 TWh globally — 25% of renewable electricity. Solar generates around 2,000 TWh — 21%. Together, they produce nearly as much electricity as all the world's hydropower. [Pause]

[Data] Solar's trajectory is extraordinary. From essentially zero in 2010, it has reached 2,000 TWh in 15 years. The cost of solar electricity has fallen by over 90% in a decade — making it, in many markets, the cheapest source of new electricity ever built.

[Benchmark] Wind has followed a similar, if slightly earlier, trajectory. Offshore wind is now expanding rapidly across Europe, East Asia, and increasingly North America.

The strategic implication is profound: the energy transition is not a linear extrapolation of past trends. It is an accelerating curve. Each year, more solar and wind capacity is added than the year before.

Key points: (1) Wind ~2,400 TWh (25%) | Solar ~2,000 TWh (21%) (2) Solar = history's fastest-growing energy technology (3) Combined wind+solar rivals hydro; trajectory suggests overtake soon
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 08_regional_disparities

[Transition] But progress at the global level can obscure a profound and troubling reality: the energy transition is deeply, systematically unequal.

Look at the map of hydropower share by country, and alongside it the electricity data. The range runs from Norway at 98% to Saudi Arabia at less than 2%. That is not a marginal difference — it is a forty-nine-fold gap. [Pause]

[Data] The leaders — Norway, Brazil, Canada — benefit from natural endowments: rivers, geography, decades of investment. Germany and Denmark have achieved high shares through determined policy: aggressive wind and solar deployment, carbon pricing, industrial transition.

[Benchmark] The laggards fall into two distinct categories. Middle Eastern nations — Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE — are fossil fuel exporters with little economic incentive, historically, to transition. Sub-Saharan Africa faces a different challenge: not lack of will, but lack of investment, grid infrastructure, and financing.

[Scan Room] For this audience, the policy implication is clear: closing regional gaps requires differentiated strategies. What works in Norway does not work in Nigeria.

Key points: (1) 98% to <2% — the range is the story (2) Leaders: hydro-rich nations + wind/solar investors (3) Laggards: fossil fuel exporters and underinvested developing economies
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 09_key_takeaways

[Transition] Let me close with five findings that should anchor your policy and strategic thinking coming out of this briefing.

First: renewables now supply approximately 14% of global primary energy and 30% of global electricity. That is real progress — but climate science tells us we need to reach 60%, 70%, 80% of electricity from renewables within this decade to stay on track for 1.5°C pathways.

Second: hydropower remains the backbone of renewable electricity at ~47%, but its growth days are largely behind it. The future is wind and solar.

Third: wind and solar are the fastest-growing energy technologies in history. The trajectory is encouraging — but the absolute scale still needs to multiply many times over.

Fourth: stark regional disparities persist. From 98% in Norway to less than 2% in Saudi Arabia. Bridging this gap is simultaneously a climate imperative and an energy justice imperative.

Fifth: transport and heating — which together constitute most of global primary energy — lag far behind electricity in the renewable transition. Electrification and green fuels must accelerate.

[Pause]

The closing thought: the transition is real. The momentum is genuine. But the pace must increase dramatically. The window to act is narrowing.

Key points: (1) Progress is real — 14% primary, 30% electricity — but pace insufficient (2) Wind + solar are the growth engines of the transition (3) Regional equity and transport/heating decarbonization are the next frontiers
Duration: 3 minutes
Flex: [If time is tight, present only the first three points and the closing statement; skip point 4 and 5 details]

We will move through the urgency of the problem, the current state of renewables in both primary energy and electricity, technology-by-technology progress, and the stark regional gaps that remain.

[Pause]

The headline: renewable energy is growing faster than at any point in history — but the pace is still insufficient to meet climate targets.

Key points: (1) Global scope — primary energy + electricity + technology breakdown (2) Data-driven, evidence-based analysis (3) The gap between progress made and progress needed
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_fossil_fuel_urgency

[Transition] To understand why renewables matter, we must first confront the scale of what we are replacing.

Three-quarters of all global greenhouse gas emissions — 75% — come from burning fossil fuels for energy. That is the foundational number driving climate policy worldwide. [Pause]

[Data] But CO₂ is only part of the story. Fossil fuel combustion also creates local air pollution that kills more than 5 million people prematurely every year. That is more than the population of New Zealand — dying annually from energy-related air quality.

[Benchmark] These figures are not theoretical projections. They are present-day realities. Fossil fuel dependence is both a long-term climate problem and an immediate public health crisis.

[Scan Room] The pathway forward is clear: a rapid shift to nuclear and renewables. This deck is about measuring how far that shift has come.

Key points: (1) 75% of GHG emissions from fossil fuels (2) 5M+ premature deaths/year from air pollution (3) Transition is urgency — not just preference
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_primary_energy_share

[Transition] So where do renewables actually stand today in the total energy picture?

Globally, approximately 14% of primary energy — roughly one-seventh — now comes from renewable technologies, using the substitution method. [Pause]

[Data] That figure reflects all energy consumed across electricity, transport, and heating combined. It is a meaningful milestone. But it also tells us that 86% of global primary energy still comes from non-renewable sources.

[Benchmark] The map on this slide shows the extraordinary variation across countries. Norway, Brazil, and New Zealand derive substantial shares of their primary energy from renewables — all driven by abundant hydropower. Meanwhile, fossil-fuel-producing nations in the Middle East and parts of Asia remain below 5%.

Why is the primary energy share lower than the electricity share we will see next? Because transport and heating — two-thirds of total energy use — are far harder to decarbonize. They still run predominantly on oil and gas.

Key points: (1) ~14% global primary energy from renewables in 2024 (2) Transport and heating lag behind electricity (3) Massive regional variation — from near-zero to majority renewable
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_generation_growth

[Transition] If primary energy shows us the full picture, electricity is where renewables have made their greatest strides.

Let me walk you through the technology breakdown of renewable electricity generation globally.

Hydropower remains the single largest source at approximately 4,500 TWh — roughly 47% of all renewable electricity. It has been generating at scale for over a century.

[Data] Wind contributes around 2,400 TWh — 25% of renewable electricity. Solar contributes around 2,000 TWh — 21%. [Pause]

[Benchmark] Here is the critical insight: wind and solar combined produce approximately 4,400 TWh — nearly matching hydro's 4,500 TWh. And unlike hydro, which has limited new sites available, wind and solar are growing dramatically.

Key points: (1) Total renewable electricity: ~9,600 TWh (2) Hydro still leads at 47%, but wind+solar now nearly equal it (3) The technology mix is shifting rapidly toward solar and wind
Duration: 2.5 minutes

---

# 05_electricity_mix

[Transition] Zooming out to the overall electricity mix: globally, almost one-third of all electricity now comes from renewable sources.

[Data] Thirty percent. That is a landmark figure — and it is substantially higher than the 14% primary energy share, precisely because electricity is the sector where renewables have made the most progress.

[Scan Room] The world map and the country table on this slide make the disparity viscerally clear. Norway generates 98% of its electricity from renewables. Brazil: 85%. Canada: 65%. These countries benefit from decades of hydropower investment.

[Benchmark] Compare that to Saudi Arabia at less than 2%. Or the many Sub-Saharan African and Middle Eastern nations below 10%. These are not small differences in degree — they are categorical differences in energy systems.

Duration: 2 minutes

---

[Pause]

[Benchmark] The strategic implication is that the renewable electricity mix of the future must be built primarily on wind and solar, not on further hydro expansion. Hydro is a foundation, not a growth engine.
